figures.finding: Lebanon taxes salaries and wages by a progressive payroll tax: 2% to LBP 360 million a year, then 4%, 7%, 11%, 15%, 20%, and 25% above LBP 13.5 billion, after family deductions; business income (a self-employed person's) is taxed separately at 4% to 25%.
figures.applies: Territorial: salary for work in Lebanon, or paid from Lebanon, or to a resident. Family deduction amounts not read.

sources.said: Family deductions are granted in calculating taxable income.
The annual progressive brackets for income tax profits became between 4% and 25%
The services that triggered the income are executed on Lebanese territory or have contributed to the welfare of a company located in Lebanon, even though the source of funding is outside Lebanon.

Article 47 - Tax on wages and salaries, and pensions. 2% Below LBP 360 million LBP; 4% Between LBP 360 million and LBP 900 million; 7% Between LBP 900 million and LBP 1,8 billion; 11% Between LBP 1,8 billion and LBP 3,6 billion; 15% Between LBP 3,6 billion and LBP7,2 billion; 20% Between LBP 7,2 billion and LBP 13,500 billion; 25% Above LBP 13,500 billion

figures.finding: An employee pays 3% to the NSSF medical scheme on pay up to LBP 120 million a month; the employer pays 8% (sickness and maternity, same ceiling), 6% family benefits (to LBP 18 million a month) and 5% end-of-service indemnity uncapped.

sources.said: 3% for the medical scheme, calculated on a maximum monthly base of LL 120 million
8% for maternity and sickness benefit schemes, calculated on a maximum monthly base of LL 120 million
6% for family benefit schemes, calculated on a maximum monthly base of LL 18 million
5% of total annual earnings for the end-of-service indemnity, with no ceiling.

figures.finding: The employer withholds payroll tax and declares it quarterly within 15 days of the quarter's end, with an annual declaration by 28 February.

sources.said: It is the employer's responsibility to declare the payroll tax to the authorities on a quarterly basis during the first 15 days of the month following the end of the quarter. An annual declaration is also due by 28 February of the following year.

figures.finding: A non-resident earning revenue from services in Lebanon bears an effective withholding of 7.5% of the revenue; royalties and technical or management fees paid to a non-resident bear 8.5%.

sources.said: Revenues earned by non-residents in Lebanon are subject to an effective WHT of 2.25% on revenue from the sale of materials and equipment, and 7.5% on the revenue in the case of sale of services.
Royalties paid to a nonresident are subject to an 8.5% withholding tax, unless the rate is reduced under an applicable tax treaty.

figures.finding: VAT is 11%; registration is required where turnover exceeds LBP 5 billion over one to four consecutive quarters.

sources.said: The standard VAT rate is 11%.
Taxpayers whose turnover exceeds LBP 5 billion for a period between one quarter and four consecutive quarters must register for VAT purposes.
Businesses with a turnover above LBP 5 billion over a period ranging from one quarter to four previous consecutive quarters (instead of LBP 100 million) are subject to mandatory registration.

figures.finding: The fiscal year is the calendar year; a self-employed person taxed on real profits files and pays before 1 April of the next year (lump-sum before 1 February).
figures.applies: Self-employed; employees are taxed through the employer.

sources.said: The fiscal year is the calendar year.
The deadline for filing tax returns for those taxed on real profits is before 1 April of the following year.

sources.said: Adjustment of tax brackets, effective from 01/01/2024 ... Article 46 - Tax on profits of commercial, industrial, and non-commercial professions: 4% Below LBP 540 million ... 25% Above LBP 13,500 billion ... Article 47 - Tax on wages and salaries, and pensions. 2% Below LBP 360 million LBP; 4% Between LBP 360 million and LBP 900 million; 7% Between LBP 900 million and LBP 1,8 billion; 11% Between LBP 1,8 billion and LBP 3,6 billion; 15% Between LBP 3,6 billion and LBP7,2 billion; 20% Between LBP 7,2 billion and LBP 13,500 billion; 25% Above LBP 13,500 billion ... Article 14 - Value Added Tax: The thresholds for businesses subject to VAT were increased as follows: Businesses with a turnover above LBP 5 billion over a period ranging from one quarter to four previous consecutive quarters (instead of LBP 100 million) are subject to mandatory registration.
